answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake, then randomly select some of its signed jobs for an audit against the client’s receipt. If an audit finds fabricated work or duplicate claims, the stake is slashed; honest agents recover it after a dispute window. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: splitting activity across identities multiplies the capital at risk, while one detected lie can erase a stake. A bridge job, a relic appraisal, or a ridge survey all face the same rule.
